🎙
President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
's
greetings
to participants and guests of the
2026 International Youth Festival
(September 13, 2026)
💬
Dear Friends! I am delighted to welcome participants and guests of the
International Youth Festival
.
This year, you have gathered in the capital of the Urals,
Yekaterinburg
– the city where Europe and Asia meet and where history literally lives in every stone.
For centuries, the Urals have produced ideas that changed our country for the better. First plants, Russia’s first industrial revolution, and hundreds of modern scientific breakthroughs. Where else but here, one of the centres of Russia’s industrial, cultural and intellectual legacy, would young leaders from different countries discuss how our life is changing with the arrival of new technology and
what kind of world we want in the future
?
🌏
🤝
In the Russian language, the word
“mir” means friendship, peace and accord
; but at the same time, it means
the world, the planet
: humanity, all the countries and peoples on Earth.
That explains so much about the
character of Russia’s multi-ethnic nation
, our decisions and actions.
If we are friends,
our friendship is strong and enduring
. If we are neighbours, we seek fairness and respect for one another.
We want every person to remain human and for their fate be determined by things other than nationality, a wallet packed with money, status or background. We strongly believe that
every nation is free to choose its path
independently and is entitled to equal access to medications, food, water, energy and education opportunities, and to the use of the latest technology that must be available to all humanity.
It is our aspiration, our cause and our dream. If you share these aspirations,
let’s change the world together
.
We will welcome those who decide to join our projects in Russia. We are equally happy to see you build our shared
new, open and, hopefully, just world
in your own home countries.
I have no doubt that you, the younger generation, will succeed.
It is your time
.
🇷🇺
Follow your dreams
with Russia
.
I wish you the best of health, good luck and all the best.

item.description: #FacesOfVictory On September 13, 1943, the leaders of the Soviet ' Young Guard ' underground resistance & youth organisation, which fought the Nazis during #WW2 in #Donbass , were awarded the title of the #HeroOfTheSovietUnion : 🌟 Ulyana Gromova 🌟 Ivan Zemnukhov 🌟 Oleg Koshevoy 🌟 Sergey Tyulenin 🌟 Lyubov Shevtsova The #YoungGuard was formed in the coalminers’ city of Krasnodon ( #Donbass ) after it had been occupied by the Nazis (July 1942). The city's residents, who found themselves in the enemy’s rear, had to mine coal — a strategic raw material for the war industry — for the needs of the Nazi troops. So, different local underground resistance groups began to fight the enemy in the city. The Young Guard underground headquarters was helmed by Ulyana Gromova , Oleg Koshevoy, Lyubov Shevtsova, Ivan Zemnukhov, Sergey Tyulenin and other boys and girls. The youngest member of the organisation — Radiy Yurkin — was only 14. On
September 13, 1943,
the leaders of the Soviet '
Young Guard
' underground resistance & youth organisation, which fought the Nazis during
#WW2
in
#Donbass
, were awarded the title of the
#HeroOfTheSovietUnion
:
🌟
Ulyana Gromova
🌟
Ivan
Zemnukhov
🌟
Oleg
Koshevoy
🌟
Sergey
Tyulenin
🌟
Lyubov
Shevtsova
The
#YoungGuard
was formed in the coalminers’ city of
Krasnodon
(
#Donbass
) after it had been occupied by the Nazis (July 1942). The city's residents, who found themselves in the enemy’s rear, had to mine coal — a strategic raw material for the war industry — for the needs of the Nazi troops. So, different
local underground resistance groups began to fight the enemy
in the city.
The Young Guard underground headquarters was helmed by
Ulyana
Gromova
,
Oleg Koshevoy, Lyubov Shevtsova, Ivan Zemnukhov, Sergey Tyulenin
and other boys and girls. The youngest member of the organisation —
Radiy Yurkin
— was only 14.
The selfless activists of the 'Young Guard', who embarked on the path of fighting against the Nazi occupants,
were no different from their peers.
They also went to school, engaged in extracurricular routine, dreamed and made plans for the future. But the
#GreatPatrioticWar
began, having changed radically their fate:
in the fight against the Nazis, they sacrificed the most valuable that they had — their lives.
The 'Young Guard' members started fighting the Nazis by making and
distributing counter-propaganda leaflets.
In December 1942, they set on fire one of the Nazi-occupied buildings in Krasnodon, where the enemy kept the lists of the people who were planned to be deported to Germany as slaves. About 2,500 young men and women of Krasnodon were
saved from the deportation.
▪️
In January 1943, shortly before fleeing from the advancing Red Army, the Nazi “polizei” intensified their efforts to eliminate the Komsomol-Communist underground resistance movement in Krasnodon. Using their informants, the Germans traced the young Soviet partisans and began mass hunt and arrests of the Young Guard members.
🖋
Excerpt from the testimony of Otto Schen —
chief of the Nazi 'polizei'
of during the occupation of Krasnodon:
During interrogations, all members of the organisation were severely tortured.
They were beaten till they fell unconscious; the polizei broke their legs and arms, then showered with cold water and threw into the cell. <...>
The prisoners’ bodies were covered with bruises and abrasions all over.
Neither torture nor brutal interrogation broke the spirit of the courageous youngsters who understood that the Nazis would not leave them alive.
They steadfastly and courageously endured, refusing to cooperate with the enemy. All the arrested members of the underground resistance
were executed on January 15, 16 and 31, 1943.
The deep pit of Coal Mine Number 5 in Krasnodon was where they were
brutally killed by the fascists.
In February 1943, Krasnodon was liberated by the Red Army. After the Nazis were expelled out of the city, local residents discovered the
mass burial
in Coal Mine 5 —
they saw a terrible picture:
a black abyss, blood, pieces of clothes and footgear. 71 bodies were taken out from the 53-meter depth of the mine.
🎖
Courageous Yong Guard members, who sacrificed their lives for Motherland, inspired thousands of their peers to perform heroic deeds during the Great Patriotic War.
The novel of the same name by writer
Alexander Fadeyev
is dedicated to the memory of the members of the "Young Guard" — the
book inspired many generations of Soviet and Russian schoolchildren
with its example of selfless devotion and self-sacrifice for the Motherland.
#WeRemember
#Victory81

🎙
President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
's
remarks
at the meeting of the 18th BRICS Summit in the
BRICS Outreach/Plus format
(September 13, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
The broad representation at today’s meeting confirms that the international community’s interest in BRICS continues to grow.
Our fundamental
values and ideals
– such as commitment to an independent and autonomous course, striving to solve problems collectively while relying on international law and the key provisions of the UN Charter –
appeal to many in the world
.
The BRICS group has always advocated that all countries without exception should have e
qual and unlimited opportunities
for consistent and balanced economic and social growth, for ensuring their populations’ wellbeing, while being able to preserve unique national cultures and traditions and to adhere to their own sovereign development models. <...>
I would like to emphasise that today BRICS is a powerful driving force behind the strengthening of
genuine multilateralism in international relations
, and plays a major role in shaping a new, fairer and
multipolar world order
.
It is worth noting that the BRICS nations are seeing steady population growth and strengthening domestic markets; they have established robust industrial, technological, financial and academic hubs, as well as modern transport, energy and digital infrastructure. Trade within our association has already reached
$1.2 trillion
. Member states account for almost a
quarter of global exports
, and it is BRICS that, at 49 percent, provides most of global GDP growth.
That said, the potential for the further development of BRICS is far from exhausted. One of the main untapped resources so far is the
complementarity of the member states’ economies
. The differences in their structure and specialisation offer vast opportunities for practical cooperation, for creating new production chains, technologies, services, and markets. <...>
I also invite everyone to take a closer look at the
promising initiatives put forward by Russia
to streamline our cooperation. These include establishing a BRICS payment, depository and clearance infrastructure, as well as setting up a reinsurance mechanism and a grain exchange within the association. I am convinced that both member states and partners of BRICS will be able to employ all these tools in the future. Further strengthening the capacity of the
BRICS New Development Bank
and updating its business model is a pressing task. <...>
Naturally, technological transformation is a key driver of global growth and sovereign development. With the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence, the development of autonomous systems, and the rise of digital trade platforms and financial solutions, the very model of economic value creation is shifting.

the consequence of systemic errors
committed by the so‑called West, or, to be more precise, by the globalist circles of the West, in the political, security and economic spheres.

this did not constitute full‑fledged membership
.

energy
. How, in fact, is the price of gas formed on the European exchanges? It is not determined by producers, but
by exchange traders
. They believe that today, it is more advantageous to extract gas from storage that was purchased at lower prices, and as for tomorrow – well, we’ll see.
This will result in prices rising not just to 1,000, but to 1,500 [dollars or euros per 1,000 cubic metres]
.
• In the security sphere, the [systemic error of the West] has taken the form of attempts to put pressure on the Russian Federation, initially through
the use of terrorists in the Caucasus
and separatists, then via other methods, and now – by means of
the neo‑Nazi regime in Ukraine
.
This process continues unabated.
• Yet today’s European elites adhere to a different perspective. They now seek to frighten their populations with a mythical Russian threat, purportedly dating back to the Soviet era. But such a threat does not exist, and never has.
👉
We do not threaten, nor do we intend to threaten, European countries
.

We met not long ago in Moscow , where we discussed matters relating to our cooperation with the New Development Bank and the Bank’s involvement. The Bank is operating energetically, doing much to advance the organisation’s development, and expanding its activities in key areas. We are very pleased that such an instrument was created at some point. We advocate the involvement of as many participants as possible in its work, and for its programmes to be broader in scope – covering a greater number of economic sectors within the #BRICS member countries. item.title: 🇷🇺 President of Russia Vladimir Putin had a conversation with Prime Minister of Malaysia
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇲🇾 President of Russia Vladimir Putin had a conversation with Prime Minister of Malaysia Anwar Ibrahim on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in India (New Delhi, September 11, 2026) 💬 Vladimir Putin : Mr Prime Minister, friends, I am very glad to see you, Mr Prime Minister. It has been a long time since our last meeting . First of all, I would like to ask you to convey my warmest regards to the Supreme Ruler of Malaysia, Sultan Ibrahim – we had the pleasure of meeting in Moscow this May at the celebrations of the 81st anniversary of Victory over Nazism . We highly appreciate the high level and truly friendly nature of relations between Russia and Malaysia. Today, we meet within the #BRICS framework – a platform where the outlines of a new, equitable and democratic world order are being shaped. We welcome Malaysia’s joining the group as a partner country , which took place during our chairmanship in 2024. Next year will mark 60 years of diplomatic relations between our countries , and we approach this significant milestone with a wealth of positive experience of cooperation and a solid foundation for its further expansion. Contacts are developing dynamically across the security councils, parliaments, foreign ministries and other relevant agencies. Recently, in August, the fifth meeting of the Joint Russian-Malaysian Commission on Economic, Scientific, Technical and Cultural Cooperation was held in Vladivostok. Last year, trade between our countries increased by 12.9 percent
